decisions.why: Rules: docs/vocabularies.md Body plans says the plan is 'the unit's upper-body shape and silhouette (legs and wheels live in mobility, scale in size)'. Casemate's meaning, 'a chassis with a forward-fixed main gun and no main turret', fits the Kaiser page: the cannon is fixed in place in an armoured housing of its own, which looks like a turret but stays locked facing forward. The Fixed-gun hull / Hull with turret tie-break says to 'decide by where the main gun sits: fixed in the hull is casemate'. Hull-turret is 'the classic tank shape, also on legs', which shows that a tank-like hull keeps its plan when it stands on legs. The vocab intro and the proposal say real units that break combination rules 'are recorded as they are' and listed as atypical; ra3.empire.mecha-tengu is a precedent (humanoid-mech on a hover-class unit, with the class break recorded). Sources: the Saxony Empire wiki page (read, not cited) says Saxon mechs often look like ordinary tanks standing on spider or crab legs. A's own fit_note calls the upper body the casemate shape. The spider-frame reading is kept in uncertain body/plan and the fit_note is kept. Flavour stays soviet under either plan.

The mode names the state, like the worked examples' 'Deployed' and 'Deployed (landed)'. The Kaiser page's gallery caption also calls it an 'Entrenched' Kaiser. Entrench stays the name of abilities/0.

Matchups convention: 'pick the link that names the part behind it'. The reason is that the cannon hits every armour class hard and out-duels any mech (Kaiser page), which is its armour-piercing damage. weapon:cannon is left for the slow-firing, small-blast weakness, so the two entries hang on different parts.

The strength is what the Entrench button adds: rocket salvos to the front and flanks, and a dug-in pair making a near-unbreakable line (Kaiser page). That is the ability's pattern, whose summary is 'gain a stronger stationary mode'.

This weakness is the anchoring itself: it cannot walk or turn, the cannon keeps only a narrow arc, and it is exposed while locking down (Kaiser page Cons). That matches the trait's meaning, 'stops to enter a stronger stationary mode; must pack up to move', and keeps it on a different part from strengths/3.

rule_problems: Body plan for a walker with a fixed-gun hull. Rule text: casemate is 'A chassis with a forward-fixed main gun and no main turret, like a tank destroyer. classes: Tank / ground vehicle, Hovercraft; only with mobility types: Wheels, Tracks, Hover; only with sizes: Medium, Large'. The vocab intro adds 'a class left out is a hard ban', and the only body tie-break that covers casemate is 'Fixed-gun hull or Hull with turret: Decide by where the main gun sits'. The Kaiser is a fixed-gun hull on four legs at huge size, so the tie-break's answer breaks three combination rules. Nothing ranks spider-frame ('a body slung between several visible legs') against casemate or hull-turret, so two coders followed the rules to different plans. The Wotan's page describes the same build (a boxy hull with a fixed turret and forward cannons on eight crab legs), so this will come up again. Proposed fix: (a) add Walker / mech to casemate's classes (rare on walker), Two legs and Many legs to its mobility types, and Huge to its sizes; (b) add a tie-break: 'Spider frame or Fixed-gun hull or Hull with turret: a walker whose upper body is a tank-like hull takes casemate or hull-turret by where its main gun sits; spider-frame is for a pod or body slung between the legs with no such hull.'

Registry note against the mode-weapon rule. Rule text: games-r3.md Wiki traps says the infobox puts ability attacks in weapon slots marked '(Ability)', names 'the Kaiser's Rockets', and says 'Record them as abilities, not weapons'. fields.md armament[].slot and armament[].mode say 'A weapon that a mode adds while the primary keeps firing is also secondary, with mode.' Both coders followed the registry. As a result, the entrenched rocket batteries, which keep firing salvos for as long as the mode lasts, exist only in words inside abilities/0, and no weapon entry records the deploy mode's main payoff (rockets family, splash, limited-arc, mode entrenched). I kept that coding and added an uncertain entry at abilities/0. Proposed fix: amend the registry bullet to '...Record them as abilities, not weapons, unless the slot is a weapon that a deploy mode uncovers and that then fires with the attack order while the mode lasts (the Kaiser's Rockets): code that as a secondary weapon with the mode, and keep the deploy button as the ability.'

Mobility traits from a veteran-only button. Rule text: mobility.traits is only 'Terms from Mobility traits', and Stock values ('Every band describes the stock unit ... no veterancy') covers bands only. By contrast, sensors.traits says 'A sensor from a loadout pick, an upgrade or veterancy goes in sensors.notes'. Both coders kept deploy-anchor, so the trait reads as stock, although an unranked Kaiser cannot entrench. I kept it and added an uncertain entry at mobility/traits. Proposed fix: add one explicit rule to mobility.traits, either 'A key-bound trait whose ability is recorded follows that ability: list it whatever the ability's source, and say in mobility.notes when it needs veterancy or an upgrade', or the sensors-style rule that moves such traits to notes.

Crew default in commanded games. Rule text, from Crew models driver-gunner: 'If the source doesn't say whether two weapons fire together, count them as one at a time.' RTS wikis rarely say this, even when each weapon plainly fires at its own target: the Kaiser's four side guns cover every side and keep firing as it walks, alongside the cannon. So both coders got solo, and the player version loses the side guns' simultaneous fire. I kept solo and added an uncertain entry at crew. Proposed fix: 'In a commanded game where the source gives each weapon its own reach and reload under one attack order, weapons on separate mounts count as firing together unless a source says otherwise.'

Many-legs speed bands. Rule text: legs-multi is 'only with speed bands: Slow, Medium, Fast, Very fast', while legs-biped allows Very slow. Iron Harvest's heaviest many-legged walkers are very slow: the Kaiser at 0.45 and the eight-legged Wotan at 0.52 of the rifle squads. Each will carry the same atypical entry, which is evidence the rule is too narrow. Proposed fix: add Very slow to legs-multi's allowed speed bands, perhaps only with sizes Large and Huge.
